title: So long as death is from sin and life was joined to righteousness by God's decree, the question matters little
source_text: XXXI. Caeterum modo constet necessitatem moriendi quae jam nobis incumbit non a natura, sed a peccato esse; & si homo in primaeva integritate perstitisset, vitam cum ejus justitia semper fuisse conjungendam, ex sapientissimo & aequissimo Dei instituto, quaestio ista non videtur ita magni esse momenti.
pass_a_gloss: But provided it be established that the necessity of dying which now lies upon us is not from nature, but from sin; and that if man had persisted in primeval integrity, life would always have been to be joined with his justice, by the most wise and most just ordinance of God, that question does not seem to be of so great moment.
pass_b_english: Still, provided it is agreed that the necessity of dying that now lies on us comes not from nature but from sin, and that had man persevered in his original integrity, life would always have been joined to his righteousness by God's most wise and most just decree, this question does not seem very important.

choices.term: non videtur ita magni esse momenti
choices.why: Le Blanc's irenic understatement; the English does not dismiss the question outright.
